title: Plural partitive demonstratives
summary: Match a plural partitive noun with näitä, noita or niitä: Etsin näitä kirjoja. — I am looking for these books.
objectives: Choose näitä, noita or niitä for a plural partitive reference.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose näitä, noita or niitä for a plural partitive reference.
The reference cue and plural meaning are visible. Match a supplied plural partitive noun, or replace an already understood collection with the demonstrative alone.
Learn nämä → näitä, nuo → noita and ne → niitä. The distance and prior-reference distinctions remain separate from the verb’s grammatical person.
keyPoints: Use näitä for these nearby things, noita for those farther away, and niitä for them or those already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.

examples.english: I am looking for these books.
steps: Use näitä for these nearby things, noita for those farther away, and niitä for them or those already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
näitä means “these” and works as the partitive demonstrative agreeing with the following noun. The standard written partitive form of nämä is näitä; learn this pronoun form directly.
kirjoja means “books” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Replace final a with o, then add -ja: kirjo- + -ja = kirjoja.

examples.english: I am looking for those cars.
steps: Use näitä for these nearby things, noita for those farther away, and niitä for them or those already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
noita means “those” and works as the partitive demonstrative agreeing with the following noun. The standard written partitive form of nuo is noita; learn this pronoun form directly.
autoja means “cars” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep auto and add -ja: auto + ja = autoja.

examples.english: I am waiting for the buses.
steps: Use näitä for these nearby things, noita for those farther away, and niitä for them or those already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.
Odotan means “I am waiting for” and works as the verb. odotan comes from odottaa: odota- + -n, with tt → t.
niitä means “them / those” and works as the partitive demonstrative agreeing with the following noun. The standard written partitive form of ne is niitä; learn this pronoun form directly.
busseja means “buses” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Change final i to e, then add -ja: busse- + -ja = busseja.

examples.english: I am looking for these cars.
steps: Use näitä for these nearby things, noita for those farther away, and niitä for them or those already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
näitä means “these” and works as the partitive demonstrative agreeing with the following noun. The standard written partitive form of nämä is näitä; learn this pronoun form directly.
autoja means “cars” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep auto and add -ja: auto + ja = autoja.

commonMistakes: Preserve the plural reference when choosing the demonstrative.
Use the reference cue as well as the case.

optionFeedback.näitä: näitä indicates several nearby references. The visible cue instead requires noita: several farther references.
